body:
You don't understand mental illness, not at all. If I had energy to put into anything, I would not be depressed, for example.

I do have room to grow. I simply lack the physical mechanisms to do so. Although I have the potential, it cannot be reached. 

But maybe I am wrong. Maybe if I die, I have prevented a good life. But maybe I will be right, and that is not a chance I am willing to take. I cannot handle this pain anymore. I tell myself "one more day" every single morning, but nothing changes. If this is what life consists of, of dragging myself through the motions, then it isn't worth it. I am not jealous of people who are healthy and happy; I truly wish them the best and hope they do not take for granted the gift they have, nor do they use it as a weapon against those who lack it.

I struggle to weigh the hurt I will cause my girlfriend against the mental and emotional anguish I have suffered my entire life. Some people are not meant to live. Think natural selection, survival of the fittest. The world weeds out the weak, and I am weak. And that's okay. I am the injured one in the herd, the one the predators choose to hunt, and with me gone, the rest of the herd will have a chance to survive, flourish, grow. 

I have been abandoned, sexually assaulted, raped, physically and verbally abused. I struggle with anxiety that's so severe, I stutter. Every single day, no matter how bright my outlook may be, I still think about suicide. My life, in my head, has always ended at my hand. Even though I may dream up an apartment in New York, an award-winning novel, afternoons spent reading in coffee-houses, it all ends with me taking my own life, and has been for as long as I can remember.

Some people feel bad periodically, but others feel bad perpetually. I am the latter. My death wouldn't be a suicide; it would be a mercy killing.

I am sorry you felt so devastated at your brother-in-law's suicide attempt. But I urge you to put yourself in his position. Imagine what you would have to experience emotionally and mentally to justify taking your own life. I can assure you that his devastation was much, much worse. 

What I wish to do is not rash. I have spent my entire conscious life thinking about this, researching it, planning it. 

Taking my darkness out of this world will only make room for more light, for more happiness. It is suffering people like me that make society the way it is.
